title: Review Manifest
description: Entry manifest for contract: review-journal/v0 - the header of a review journal. Declares the review, its panel, and its classification ceiling. The ceiling is set by the org's cxotech agent or the maintainer (ROE), is never set by the author, and bounds what evidence any journal entry may carry: an entry's classification must not exceed the ceiling (a journal-set property, checked across the manifest and event stream together).

reasoner.description: The reasoner (model) behind a participant, or the literal string 'not-exposed'. The field MUST admit non-exposure: a harness that does not expose its reasoner records 'not-exposed' rather than inventing a value.

capabilities.description: Host-less capability tokens. Must include the exact review-journal contract token.

ref.description: Branch, PR, or commit under review.

seats.description: The panel roster. Each seat records the role prompt it ran under - the framing axis is the standard's primary hardening lever - and the participant occupying it, which is what joins events to prompt and reasoner for variance comparison. A roster of only author seats is not a panel: at least one non-author seat is required, because a declared panel with no approving seat at all would otherwise conform. Seat names MUST be unique within the roster (v0 has no multi-occupant key, so a duplicated seat makes the event join ambiguous); JSON Schema cannot express that uniqueness, so it is enforced by the journal-set check. The maintainer seat's participant MUST be human - final merge authority is a human, per the standard's non-negotiable.

seat.description: Role seat. Same constraint as the event seat - a roster cannot declare a seat no event can reference.

participant.description: The participant occupying this seat. Events join to it via agent.participant_ref. One participant may occupy multiple seats; the join is what lets a checker prove the same participant does not both author and approve.

execution.description: How this seat was actually run - the launch composition behind the participant. Optional in v0 (reserve-don't-force); the standard (section 9.2) makes it REQUIRED for every compared seat when a framing-comparison claim is made from the journal - a bound the schema cannot see, because the claim lives outside the file. All references are SYMBOLIC: tokens resolved against an operator-maintained launch matrix, never command lines, flags, or filesystem paths - raw launch detail drifts with tool versions and is the part of a seat record most likely to carry non-public operating detail.

harness.description: Symbolic harness token - the class or product token under which the seat ran (e.g. an orchestrator-native subagent facility or a headless vendor CLI), resolved by the operator's matrix. Never an invocation string.

profile_ref.description: Symbolic reference to the operator-provisioned launch/permission profile the seat ran under. Omitted when the harness runs without one; when present it names the profile, never its contents.

environment_ref.description: Symbolic reference to the environment composition (credentials, variables) the seat ran under - a token from the operator's matrix, or 'inherited' for a seat running in the launching operator's own session environment. Names the composition, never its contents. This is the environment layer of the composition model; the working-tree layer is carried per disposition by the standard's exact-head rule, not here.

mode.description: interactive: a live multi-turn session. headless: a non-interactive single-turn or scripted run. subagent: spawned inside an orchestrating session, sharing its working tree.

capture.description: How the seat's output entered the record. Deliberately admits no terminal-scrape form: a truncated terminal tail loses structure and can cut mid-finding, so it is not a capture method this contract recognizes.

role_prompt.description: The named role prompt this seat ran under. digest is required for approving AGENT review seats - every seat that must carry role_prompt at all: a version pin carries semantic identity, not byte identity, so {slug, version} alone can name two materially different prompts, and the digest proves which framing the seat actually ran under. The author and maintainer seats are outside this requirement by design: the author's prompt frames no approval, and the maintainer is the human merge authority, not a prompted review seat.

digest.description: sha256 of the resolved prompt bytes, prefixed so the label names the algorithm.

ceiling.description: The declared content-level ceiling. The cross-enum floor access_tier >= sensitivity is enforced below per the minimum-access-tier-per-sensitivity table in docs/standards/access-tier-classification.md#relationship-to-sensitivity; 'unknown' is valid only as a pair. set_by names the seat that set the ceiling - a first-class field, never inferred from who posted first - and may not be the author seat (standard section 10). The journal-set check requires set_by to resolve to exactly one declared roster seat and verifies at the person level that the setter's participant is not an author participant; a setter that resolves to no participant is a failure, not a pass.

set_by.description: The seat that set this ceiling. Never the author seat.
